o: Two cups per hour and 16 cups per day
No more than 6 cups per hour and 48 cups per day
Eight cups per hour and 64 cups per day
No hourly limit if intake is water
why: AFH 1 advises limiting fluids to no more than six cups an hour and 48 cups a day.

q: What minimum distances apply to designated tobacco-use areas on USAF installations?
o: 25 feet from entrances and 50 feet from playgrounds
50 feet from entrances but no minimum from air intakes
At least 50 feet from building entrances and air intakes, and at least 100 feet from playgrounds
At least 100 feet from every building and 200 feet from playgrounds
why: Designated areas must be at least 50 feet from entrances and air intakes and 100 feet from playgrounds.

q: What is the consequence for a military member who ingests prohibited products containing or derived from hemp seed, hemp seed oil, or CBD?
o: The member receives a fitness exemption
The conduct is permitted if the product was sold commercially
The conduct results only in nutrition counseling
Failure to comply violates Article 92, UCMJ
why: Ingestion is prohibited for readiness and drug-testing reasons; noncompliance violates Article 92, UCMJ.

q: Within what period must ADAPT program managers review medical records and documentation after notification?
o: Within seven calendar days
Within 30 calendar days
Before the member's next performance report closes
Only after the commander requests a clinical review
why: ADAPT program managers conduct the required review within seven calendar days of notification.

q: Into which four categories do stress reactions typically fall?
o: Personal, professional, family, and financial
Cognitive, emotional, behavioral, and physical
Acute, chronic, traumatic, and operational
Mental, physical, social, and spiritual
why: Stress reactions are categorized as cognitive, emotional, behavioral, and physical.

q: Which four wellness domains make up Comprehensive Airman Fitness?
o: Readiness, resilience, recovery, and reconstitution
Cognitive, emotional, behavioral, and physical
Mental, physical, social, and spiritual
Awareness, adaptability, endurance, and communication
why: CAF is a holistic approach encompassing mental, physical, social, and spiritual wellness.

q: What is military protocol?
o: An informal set of locally preferred social practices
A system used only for foreign diplomatic events
A drill manual governing formation movements
A code of traditional precedence, courtesy, and etiquette for military, diplomatic, official, and celebratory ceremonies
why: Military protocol applies traditional precedence, courtesy, and etiquette to official and ceremonial life.

q: What is the primary mission of today's base honor guard program?
o: To provide professional military funeral honors for active members, retirees, and Air Force veterans
To conduct every installation promotion ceremony
To train only Security Forces members in drill
To support only ceremonies in the National Capital Region
why: The base honor guard's primary mission is professional funeral honors for active, retired, and veteran Air Force members.

q: At minimum, what funeral ceremony has public law provided for all veterans since January 2000?
o: A firing party and military band
Folding and presentation of a U.S. flag and the playing of Taps
A full honor guard and caisson
A flyover and burial at a national cemetery
why: The statutory minimum includes folding the flag, presenting it to the family, and playing Taps.

q: On a USAF installation, what should a moving vehicle do when the national anthem or To the Colors begins?
o: Continue at reduced speed until the music ends
Stop immediately in the traffic lane regardless of safety
Pull safely to the side and stop, when consistent with safety and mission requirements; occupants sit quietly
Only government vehicles must stop
why: Vehicles pull to the side and stop when safe and mission-compatible, and occupants remain seated quietly through the last note.

q: How should a uniformed military member without headgear act indoors during the national anthem?
o: Salute regardless of headgear
Place the right hand over the heart
Face away from the music if no flag is displayed
Stand at attention without saluting
why: Indoors without headgear, a uniformed member stands at attention but does not salute.

q: At an outdoor event where the Pledge of Allegiance is rendered, what do military personnel in uniform do?
o: Stand at attention, remain silent, face the flag, and salute
Recite the pledge while holding the salute
Stand at parade rest without saluting
Remove headgear and place the right hand over the heart
why: Uniformed personnel outdoors stand at attention, remain silent, face the flag, and salute.

q: What do the 13 white stars and the yellow numerals 1947 on the DAF Seal represent?
o: The first 13 Air Force major commands and the year of the first flight
The original 13 colonies and the year the Department of the Air Force was established
The 13 original states and the year the USAF became a combatant command
The 13 stripes of the flag and the year the Air Corps was created
why: The stars represent the original colonies, and 1947 marks establishment of the Department of the Air Force.

q: What do the six sections of the stylized wings in the official Air Force Symbol represent?
o: The six enlisted tiers
Six core values shared by the services
Air and space superiority, global attack, rapid global mobility, precision engagement, information superiority, and agile combat support
The six geographic combatant commands
why: The six wing sections symbolize six distinctive Air Force capabilities listed in AFH 1.

q: What do the five points of the star in the Air Force Symbol represent?
o: The five military services existing in 1947
Five stages of aerospace power
Five Air Force core missions
RegAF, civilians, Guard, Reserve, and retirees
why: The five points represent the five components of the Air Force family: RegAF, civilians, Guard, Reserve, and retirees.

q: What is required when the Air Force song is played?
o: Airmen stand at attention and may sing the lyrics
Airmen salute from the first note through the last
Only the official party stands
Airmen remain seated unless outdoors
why: Airmen stand at attention during the Air Force song, but they are allowed to sing.

q: Which statement about folding the United States flag is official policy?
o: Each fold has an official meaning prescribed by DAFI 90-1202
There is no official meaning for the folds and no official flag-folding script
The 13 folds officially represent the original colonies
A narrative used by civic groups is required at military ceremonies
why: DAFI 90-1202 assigns neither official meanings to the folds nor an official folding script.

q: Which flag is used as an alternative to the installation flag during inclement weather?
o: The 3-by-4-foot all-purpose rayon flag
The 20-by-38-foot garrison flag
The 5-foot-by-9-foot-6-inch all-purpose all-weather storm flag
The 4-foot-4-inch-by-5-foot-6-inch ceremonial flag
why: The lightweight nylon all-weather storm flag, 5 feet by 9 feet 6 inches, is the inclement-weather alternative.

q: When may the United States flag be displayed 24 hours a day?
o: Only on federal holidays
Whenever the installation commander is present
Only if every other flag is lowered at sunset
When a patriotic effect is desired and the flag is properly illuminated during darkness
why: Continuous display is permitted for patriotic effect when the flag is illuminated during hours of darkness.

q: Where is the United States flag placed on a stage?
o: On the flag's own right, which is the audience's left
On the audience's right regardless of other flags
At the center behind the speaker in every case
On the lowest staff so other flags remain visible
why: The U.S. flag occupies its own right; to an audience facing the stage, that is the audience's left.

q: When a United States flag passes in a procession, when does a uniformed member salute?
o: Only while the flag is directly in front of the member
Six paces before it passes until it has passed six paces
From the first audible drumbeat until the procession ends
Three paces before it passes until the flag is out of sight
why: The salute begins six paces before the flag passes and is held until it is six paces beyond the member.

q: Which is the correct order of precedence for these service flags?
o: Army, National Guard, Navy, Marine Corps, Coast Guard, Air Force, Space Force
National Guard, Army, Marine Corps, Navy, Air Force, Coast Guard, Space Force
National Guard, Army, Navy, Marine Corps, Coast Guard, Air Force, Space Force
Army, Navy, Marine Corps, National Guard, Coast Guard, Air Force, Space Force
why: Precedence follows service dates: National Guard, Army, Navy, Marine Corps, Coast Guard, Air Force, then Space Force.

q: How do military personnel enter and exit automobiles or small boats when rank determines the order?
o: The senior enters first and exits last
The senior enters and exits first
Juniors enter and exit first
Juniors enter first; the senior enters last and exits first
why: Personnel enter in reverse rank order, placing the senior last to enter and first to exit.

q: How are retirees addressed in official records and correspondence?
o: By their retired grade, except in matters related to civilian employment
By first and last name without grade
By their final duty title instead of grade
By retired grade only for the first year after retirement
why: Retirees retain their grade in official records and correspondence except when the matter concerns civilian employment.

q: When formally reporting to an officer indoors, where does the member halt before saluting and reporting?
o: One pace from the doorway
Approximately two paces from the officer or desk
Six paces from the officer
At the position where the officer first makes eye contact
why: The reporting member marches to about two paces from the officer or desk, halts, salutes, and reports.

q: Who renders salutes when members are in formation or a work detail?
o: Every member independently
Only commissioned officers in the group
The person in charge salutes for the formation or detail
No one may salute under either circumstance
why: Individuals do not salute independently; the person in charge acknowledges salutes for the formation or work detail.

q: How far in advance should planners aim to have event details completed so guests can plan?
o: At least three duty days
Exactly one month
No earlier than invitations are issued
At least three weeks, or more
why: AFH 1 advises completing details at least three weeks ahead, with larger events beginning much earlier.

q: When is a promotion ceremony customarily held when the promotion takes effect on the first day of the month?
o: On the last duty day before the effective date
On the first duty day after the effective date
Exactly one week before the effective date
Only during the next commander's call
why: Because most promotions take effect on the first, ceremonies are customarily held on the preceding last duty day.

q: Which rule applies when administering a reenlistment oath?
o: The oath may be administered by video if both parties are in uniform
The reenlistee and administering officer must be physically collocated, and 'so help me God' may be omitted if desired
The words 'so help me God' are mandatory
Only the member's commander may administer the oath
why: The officer and reenlistee must be physically together; the closing religious phrase may be omitted.

q: What are the two purposes of the retreat ceremony?
o: To start the duty day and raise the flag
To assemble the unit and announce the next day's schedule
To signal the end of the official duty day and pay respect to the United States flag
To lower the flag and dismiss only the honor guard
why: Retreat marks the end of the official duty day and serves as a ceremony of respect for the flag.

q: What is the key distinction between a dining-in and a dining-out?
o: A dining-in is informal, while a dining-out is formal
A dining-out requires utility uniforms
A dining-in includes civilians but excludes spouses
A dining-in is for military members only; nonmilitary spouses, friends, and civilians may attend a dining-out
why: Both are formal, but attendance at a dining-in is limited to military members, while a dining-out may include civilian guests.

q: Your section missed a monthly target because of a preventable scheduling error you made. The dashboard is due in an hour, and changing one entry would make the section appear compliant. What is the MOST effective action?
o: Report the result accurately, acknowledge your error, and propose corrective action
Change the entry now and correct it quietly after the leadership meeting
Omit the target from the dashboard because the miss was preventable
Ask a subordinate to decide whether the entry should be changed
why: AFH 1, 1.3.1 identifies honesty and accountability as virtues of Integrity First: Airmen accurately report performance, maintain transparency, and own the outcomes of their decisions.

q: Two equally qualified Airmen request the same desirable schedule. One is a longtime friend, while the other recently joined the flight. Which action is the LEAST effective?
o: Apply the same mission-based criteria to both requests and explain the decision
Approve your friend's request because the established relationship makes the choice easier
Ask another leader to review the decision if your impartiality could reasonably be questioned
Explore whether an alternate schedule can meet both Airmen's needs without harming the mission
why: AFH 1, 1.1 requires fair and unbiased treatment and genuine dignity, fairness, and respect. Favoring a friend substitutes personal preference for impartial standards.

q: A vendor whose contract you help monitor offers you an expensive dinner after a successful project. The vendor says no future business will be discussed. What is the MOST effective action?
o: Accept because the project is complete and discuss only personal topics
Attend but pay for part of the meal after the vendor orders
Decline the offer and seek ethics guidance if any question remains
Send a junior Airman in your place so the relationship with the vendor remains strong
why: AFH 1, 1.4 states that public service is a public trust, warns against gifts from entities doing business with the agency, and requires conduct that avoids even the appearance of impropriety.

q: You recommended a different course of action, but your commander selected a lawful plan you believe is less efficient. Which action is the LEAST effective?
o: Clarify the commander's intent, then execute the decision professionally
Use the chain of command to offer new evidence if it materially changes the situation
Help your team understand the plan without pretending your earlier concerns never existed
Tell the team the plan is misguided and encourage them to delay it until the commander reconsiders
why: AFH 1, 1.3.2 explains that loyalty includes executing leaders' lawful decisions even when we disagree and offering alternatives most effectively through the chain of command.

q: A reliable teammate is temporarily overwhelmed by two urgent tasks, while you have finished your own work early. What is the MOST effective action?
o: Coordinate priorities and help carry the workload while preserving accountability for the tasks
Wait to see whether the teammate misses a deadline before offering assistance
Take over both tasks without telling the teammate or supervisor
Remind the teammate that everyone is responsible for carrying an equal share
why: AFH 1, 1.3.3 describes teamwork as giving one's best, motivating others, carrying one's own weight, and helping wingmen carry theirs when necessary.

q: After approving a flawed schedule, you realize your decision caused avoidable overtime. Which response is the LEAST effective?
o: Tell the affected team what happened and correct the schedule
Let the team assume the scheduling system caused the problem so confidence in you is preserved
Ask for constructive feedback on how to prevent a recurrence
Document the lesson and take ownership when briefing your supervisor
why: AFH 1, 1.3.1 requires accountable Airmen to maintain transparency, seek honest feedback, and own the outcomes of their actions and decisions. Concealing responsibility violates that principle.

q: A promotion-eligible Airman will be away for the entire testing cycle on a scheduled mission. The departure date is approaching. What is the MOST effective action?
o: Wait until the Airman returns and request supplemental consideration
Ask the unit to excuse the Airman from testing because the absence is mission-related
Coordinate for the Airman to test before departure if the correct test materials are available
Have the Airman test remotely while away using locally available study references
why: AFH 1, 9.10 says members unavailable for the entire testing cycle must be prepared to test before departure and may test early when the correct test booklets are available.

q: A promotion-eligible coworker wants convenient access to personal flash cards during lunch. Which action is the LEAST effective?
o: Keep the flash cards on a personally owned device authorized for personal use
Use the government computer only to view official electronic study references
Study the personal flash cards away from government information systems
Upload the personal flash cards to a government shared drive marked as private
why: AFH 1, 9.11 prohibits creating, storing, or transferring personal promotion-study notes on government computers; those systems may be used only to view official electronic study references.

q: While reviewing your Data Verification Record, you find an incorrect award entry shortly before the promotion cutoff. What is the MOST effective action?
o: Immediately contact the military personnel flight, provide supporting information, and verify the updated record afterward
Correct your local copy and retain it in case the board asks for evidence
Wait for the promotion results before raising the issue to avoid unnecessary work
Ask your supervisor to mention the award informally to board members
why: AFH 1, 9.14 requires eligible Airmen to review the DVR, immediately contact the military personnel flight about errors or omissions, and verify that corrections were completed accurately.

q: A supervisor asks to see an Airman's promotion score notice to compare the shop's results. The Airman has not provided written consent. Which action is the LEAST effective?
o: Use published promotion statistics for general comparison instead of the individual's notice
Give the notice to the supervisor because supervisors are responsible for professional development
Explain that the individual can retrieve and review the notice personally
Refer any authorized command review to the commander and limit use to notification or advisory counseling
why: AFH 1, 9.21 restricts promotion score notices to the individual and commander; supervisors are not authorized access, and scores require the Airman's written consent for disclosure.

q: A quiet junior Airman privately identifies a recurring process weakness but fears being dismissed during the team meeting. What is the MOST effective action?
o: Present the idea as your own so the team evaluates it without bias
Ask the Airman to wait until gaining more experience before challenging the process
Create space for the Airman to explain the concern, evaluate it on its merits, and protect respectful discussion
Keep the concern private unless the weakness causes a mission failure
why: AFH 1, 14.1 teaches that trust-based teams permit open, honest communication and allow members to take risks and share ideas without fear of being shut down or discounted.

q: Two work centers disagree over access to a limited training resource, and both have legitimate mission needs. Which action is the LEAST effective?
o: Bring both sides together to identify interests and explore a shared schedule
Use objective mission priorities to frame a solution both sides can support
Ask each side to explain constraints and search for a mutually beneficial option
Use rank to impose your preferred allocation before hearing either side's concerns
why: AFH 1, 14.5 describes collaboration as high in assertiveness and cooperation and aimed at satisfying both sides through honest discussion; forcing relies on authority or power with low cooperation.

q: An Airman handles a difficult customer exceptionally well and prevents a mission delay. What is the MOST effective supervisory response?
o: Provide specific positive feedback as close to the event as possible and connect it to future performance
Save the feedback for the next annual evaluation so it carries more weight
Praise the whole flight generally to avoid singling out one person
Say nothing unless the Airman asks how the interaction went
why: AFH 1, 14.13 states that successful counseling occurs as close to the event as possible and that leaders should use naturally occurring events to provide feedback, including for superior performance.

q: An experienced Airman asks for help choosing between two realistic development paths. There is time for a thoughtful discussion. What is the MOST effective counseling approach?
o: Select the path you would choose and direct the Airman to follow it
Listen, help the Airman clarify priorities and options, and support the Airman's own sound decision
Avoid discussing the decision so the Airman develops complete independence
Ask the Airman's peers to vote on which path is best
why: AFH 1, 14.14 prefers the nondirective approach for most counseling: the leader listens and helps the Airman explore and clarify the situation rather than supplying the solution.

q: You must counsel an Airman about a pattern of missed suspense dates. Which action is the LEAST effective?
o: State the purpose, discuss the issue, develop a realistic plan, and record it
Choose a setting with minimal interruptions and explain the meeting's purpose in advance
Conduct the discussion in a busy common area and end once you have listed the Airman's mistakes
Set a tentative follow-up before closing the session
why: AFH 1, 14.15 calls for an appropriate, distraction-free environment and four counseling components: state the purpose, discuss issues, develop a plan of action, and record the plan, with follow-up as appropriate.

q: A high-performing Airman is unsure how current strengths connect to long-term career goals. What is the MOST effective action?
o: Wait for the Airman to choose a goal independently before discussing development
Recommend the same career plan that worked for you
Focus only on the next promotion because long-range plans change frequently
Discuss performance, potential, goals, and development options, then continue mentoring as the plan evolves
why: AFH 1, 14.9 makes mentoring an ongoing leadership responsibility and directs supervisors to discuss performance, potential, professional development, personal goals, assignments, and long-range plans.

q: Your reports show that output is acceptable, but Airmen mention equipment problems that never appear in formal metrics. What is the MOST effective action?
o: Visit the work center, observe conditions firsthand, invite unresolved problems, and prioritize the issues that most affect success
Rely on the reports because direct observation could signal distrust
Tell Airmen to submit more metrics before you become involved
Address only problems that have already caused a missed mission
why: AFH 1, 14.22 advises leaders to get out from behind the desk, see conditions firsthand, search out problems, encourage people to raise them, and focus involvement on critical issues.

q: An installation warning directs personnel to avoid a specific area and await protective-action instructions. A coworker thinks it is probably only an exercise. Which action is the LEAST effective?
o: Follow the warning and monitor official channels for updated directions
Enter the restricted area briefly to determine whether the warning is real
Help nearby personnel understand the communicated protective action
Use the installation's mass-notification information rather than rumors
why: AFH 1, 17.6 requires personnel to respond to directions communicated through mass warning and notification systems when an incident is imminent or in progress.

q: A nearby hazardous-material release is not yet fully characterized, and evacuation could move personnel toward the hazard. The installation directs shelter-in-place. What is the MOST effective action?
o: Evacuate immediately using the shortest route, regardless of the direction of the release
Open windows so occupants can detect when the air clears
Shelter as directed, close windows and doors, turn off ventilation, and await official guidance
Send one person outside periodically to assess conditions
why: AFH 1, 17.9 explains that shelter-in-place may be required when the hazard is unknown or evacuation is dangerous and directs occupants to close windows and doors and turn off ventilation to prevent contamination.

q: During an exercise, you observe several unidentified vehicles conducting suspicious surveillance near a controlled area. What is the MOST effective action?
o: Post the observation in the unit group chat so others can identify the vehicles
Wait until the exercise ends to avoid distracting the control center
Report only the vehicle count because interpretations could be wrong
Immediately send a secure SALUTE report with size, activity, location, unit or identifying features, time, and equipment
why: AFH 1, 17.12 directs personnel who observe an attack or enemy movement to report it immediately through the chain using the secure SALUTE format.

q: You find an exposed electrical conductor in a work area. You cannot safely eliminate the hazard immediately. What is the MOST effective action?
o: Keep personnel away, promptly notify the supervisor or safety office, and submit a hazard report
Mention it at the next staff meeting if no one is injured
Cover it with an unapproved material and consider the hazard eliminated
Leave an anonymous note near the conductor without notifying an agency
why: AFH 1, 17.16 requires notification to the safety office, responsible supervisor, or local agency and submission of a hazard report when a hazard cannot be eliminated immediately.

q: A time-sensitive task now carries more risk than the approved plan anticipated, and the remaining risk exceeds your authority to accept. Which action is the LEAST effective?
o: Pause at a safe point and elevate the risk decision to the appropriate authority
Accept the additional risk yourself because stopping could make the section look unresponsive
Engage experienced personnel to identify lower-risk ways to meet the mission
Explain the changed hazard and available controls to the decision authority
why: AFH 1, 17.19 requires accepting no unnecessary risk and making risk decisions at the appropriate level; mission pressure does not expand an individual's risk-acceptance authority.

q: While a planned outdoor task is underway, winds suddenly increase and begin moving unsecured equipment. What is the MOST effective action?
o: Continue because the original deliberate risk assessment already approved the task
Wait for a formal written assessment before responding to the change
Reassess the changing situation in real time, apply immediate controls, and elevate if the residual risk requires it
Let each Airman independently decide whether the task remains safe
why: AFH 1, 17.22 describes real-time risk management as rapidly identifying and assessing hazards in a new or changing situation, selecting controls, and acting at the appropriate level.

q: Several harmless-looking public posts from your unit, when combined, reveal a predictable surge schedule. Which action is the LEAST effective?
o: Treat the pattern as a possible operations-security indicator and notify the proper program channel
Review which signatures and associations allowed the schedule to be inferred
Reduce or alter unnecessary indicators while preserving authorized communication
Leave the posts unchanged because no single post contains the complete schedule
why: AFH 1, 18.8 explains that adversaries can piece together friendly actions and open-source indicators through signatures, associations, and profiles to derive critical information.

q: You receive Controlled Unclassified Information for an official task and need a teammate's help. What is the MOST effective action?
o: Confirm the teammate's authorized need and use approved safeguarding and dissemination methods
Send it through a personal account because the information is not classified
Remove the CUI marking and share only the pages you think are relevant
Place it on an unrestricted shared drive so the teammate can retrieve it
why: AFH 1, 18.11 defines CUI as government information requiring safeguarding or dissemination controls and states that it must be protected under national policy.

q: You find classified material unattended and outside proper control. Which action is the LEAST effective?
o: Take custody of the material and safeguard it
Leave it in place and email the work center asking whoever owns it to retrieve it
Immediately notify your commander, supervisor, or security manager
Limit further access while the incident is addressed
why: AFH 1, 18.12 requires anyone finding classified material out of proper control to take custody, safeguard it, and immediately notify the commander, supervisor, or security manager.

q: A colleague asks you for personal information from an official system of records to help plan a private recognition event. What is the MOST effective action?
o: Provide only the fields that seem harmless
Share the information verbally so no record of disclosure is created
Decline unless disclosure is authorized by consent or an applicable Privacy Act provision, and use an authorized alternative
Export the record but ask the colleague to delete it after the event
why: AFH 1, 18.15 states that the Privacy Act generally prohibits disclosure from a system of records without the subject's written consent and governs federal use and dissemination of personal information.

q: A mission team wants to use a personally purchased wireless tablet to process Department of Defense information during travel. Which action is the LEAST effective?
o: Use only a device and connection method approved for processing the information
Verify documented approval and applicable user restrictions before use
Secure approved devices when they are not assigned or in use
Use the personal tablet temporarily because operational urgency outweighs the approval requirement
why: AFH 1, 18.20 requires approval of wireless systems, devices, applications, and connection methods before they process Department of Defense information.

q: A package in the mailroom has no return address, oily stains, protruding wire, and an unusual odor. What is the MOST effective action?
o: Do not open or cut it; report it immediately, control exposure, and identify who was present
Move it through the building to an office where a supervisor can inspect it
Cut one corner carefully to determine whether it contains a harmless spill
Return it through normal mail channels without documenting who handled it
why: AFH 1, 18.27 says never cut wrappings on a suspect package, report suspicious mail immediately, and make a list of personnel who were present when it was identified.

q: While deployed, a general order prohibits an activity that is legal at home but conflicts with host-nation sensitivities. Which action is the LEAST effective?
o: Comply and ensure your Airmen understand the restriction
Treat the restriction as optional because the activity is lawful in the United States
Ask the chain of command for clarification if the order's application is unclear
Explain that discipline and host-nation relations support the mission
why: AFH 1, 19.3 requires compliance with deployed general orders tailored to local laws, customs, and mission needs; strict compliance supports discipline, host-nation relations, and operations.

q: During an operation, a leader gives a clearly illegal order to mistreat a protected detainee. What is the MOST effective action?
o: Obey now and challenge the order only after the operation
Ask another Airman to carry it out so you are not personally involved
Refuse the clearly illegal order and promptly report the suspected law-of-war violation to proper authority
Remain silent unless the detainee submits a formal complaint
why: AFH 1, 19.9 states that the duty to comply with the law of war includes refusing clearly illegal orders and promptly reporting suspected violations to the commander or other proper authority.

q: A hostile actor stops the threatening action and begins complying with clear directions. Which response is the LEAST effective under the self-defense principles described in AFH 1?
o: Reassess whether a hostile act or hostile intent still exists
Use de-escalation when time and circumstances permit
Limit any force to what is reasonable in nature, duration, and scope for the threat
Continue using force to punish the actor and discourage future misconduct
why: AFH 1, 19.10 requires de-escalation when feasible and limits self-defense force to the amount necessary and reasonable to counter the threat, not punishment after the threat ceases.

q: You observe two Airmen commit the same minor standards violation; one is your strongest performer. What is the MOST effective action?
o: Apply the standard consistently, consider relevant facts fairly, and correct both in a timely manner
Correct only the weaker performer because the stronger Airman has earned flexibility
Ignore both violations to avoid appearing selective
Publicly punish the stronger performer more severely to prove impartiality
why: AFH 1, 19.4 requires standards to be uniformly known, consistently applied, and non-selectively enforced; accountability is essential to good order and discipline.

q: A Regular Air Force member strongly supports a partisan candidate and is invited to help at a campaign rally. Which action is the LEAST effective?
o: Vote and express a personal opinion in a manner that does not imply Air Force endorsement
Give a campaign speech at the partisan rally while off duty and out of uniform
Review the political-activity restrictions before participating in any event
Attend only in a manner permitted for a spectator and avoid active campaign management
why: AFH 1, 20.13 prohibits RegAF members from participating in partisan rallies, campaign speeches, fundraising, management, conventions, or debates even when out of uniform.

q: A supervisor develops a close personal financial arrangement with a directly rated subordinate, and coworkers now question whether assignments are fair. What is the MOST effective action?
o: Keep the arrangement private as long as performance ratings remain unchanged
Tell coworkers that relationships outside duty hours can never be an official concern
Address the relationship through the chain, remove actual or perceived favoritism, and restore professional boundaries
Rotate unpopular tasks among the other Airmen until concerns fade
why: AFH 1, 20.17 makes relationships an official concern when they adversely affect or reasonably could affect morale, discipline, respect for authority, cohesion, or mission accomplishment.

q: You learn that repeated comments in the shop may constitute unlawful discriminatory harassment. What is the MOST effective supervisory action?
o: Wait for the targeted Airman to file a formal complaint before intervening
Ask the entire shop to settle the issue informally without leadership involvement
Move the targeted Airman to another shift as the first response
Take immediate and appropriate action to address the allegation and consult the Equal Opportunity office
why: AFH 1, 20.18 charges commanders and supervisors to take immediate, appropriate action once aware of inappropriate behavior or allegations and encourages consultation with the Equal Opportunity office.

q: A rumor alleges that an Airman committed misconduct, but the available evidence is conflicting and you have not reviewed the member's record. Which action is the LEAST effective?
o: Issue the harshest reprimand immediately to demonstrate zero tolerance, regardless of the evidence
Determine whether the greater weight of credible evidence establishes the misconduct
Consider the nature and seriousness of the incident and the member's prior disciplinary record
Use a corrective tool intended to improve, correct, and instruct if the facts support action
why: AFH 1, 20.25 bases corrective action on the incident's nature and seriousness, prior disciplinary history, and a preponderance of credible evidence; unsupported punishment may be legally unsustainable.

q: An Airman on flying status wants to begin a performance supplement with a proprietary blend and no listed ingredient amounts. What is the MOST effective action?
o: Begin with half the label dose because supplements are tested before sale
Consult the flight surgeon before taking it and evaluate third-party verification and undeclared-ingredient risk
Use it only on non-flying days without informing medical personnel
Rely on online reviews from other service members who used the product
why: AFH 1, 22.16 warns that performance supplements may contain undeclared ingredients, notes that the FDA does not test them before sale, and requires Airmen on flying status to consult their flight surgeon.

q: An Airman has several unexplained absences and behavior changes and acknowledges increasing alcohol use. What is the MOST effective supervisory action?
o: Diagnose a substance use disorder and prescribe a recovery plan yourself
Ignore the admission unless an alcohol-related incident occurs on duty
Document specific observations, discuss them with the appropriate leadership, and facilitate professional assessment while maintaining standards
Remove all duties permanently before any professional assessment
why: AFH 1, 22.23 directs leaders to discuss documented behavior and acknowledged substance-use concerns with the supervisor, first sergeant, or commander to expedite care; ADAPT personnel, not supervisors, diagnose disorders.

q: A capable Airman reports persistent stress symptoms and asks whether seeking mental health care will end a promising career. Which action is the LEAST effective?
o: Treat the concern seriously and help the Airman identify an appropriate support resource
Explain that early help can improve recovery, judgment, and performance
Protect the Airman's dignity while continuing appropriate mission and supervisory support
Warn the Airman that seeking care usually damages a career and advise waiting until performance collapses
why: AFH 1, 22.33 calls help-seeking a sign of strength and good judgment and explains that early care improves recovery and can improve performance or preserve a career.
